# How much of your paycheck can be garnished?

> Free tool: enter your pay stub and see the most that can be garnished from your paycheck under federal law for a debt judgment, a defaulted student loan or child support, how much is protected, and a draft request for payroll's worksheet. Runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded.

Free and open source (MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## The federal limits it applies

- Ordinary debt judgment: the lesser of 25% of disposable earnings or the amount above 30 times the federal minimum wage ($7.25). Nothing can be garnished from disposable pay at or below $217.50 a week, $435 every two weeks, $471.25 twice a month or $942.50 a month (15 U.S.C. 1673(a); 29 CFR 870.10; U.S. Department of Labor Fact Sheet #30, checked 2026-11-13).
- Child support or alimony: 50% if the worker supports another spouse or child, 60% if not, 5 points more for arrears over 12 weeks (15 U.S.C. 1673(b)).
- Defaulted federal student loan (administrative garnishment): 15% (31 CFR 285.11; 34 CFR 34.4).
- Federal law is a floor: many states protect more. Tax levies and bankruptcy plans follow other rules and are not modelled.
